label: Organization
definition: Any legal entity participating in grantmaking or philanthropy. An organization occupies one or more contextual roles (see Organization Role) rather than being permanently classified as a funder or a recipient.

label: Organization Role
definition: A contextual capacity an organization occupies within a specific arrangement or award -- such as acting as a funder, grant recipient, or fiscal sponsor -- rather than a permanent trait of the organization itself.

label: Organization Type
definition: The legal and tax classification of what an organization fundamentally is (e.g., a public charity, private foundation, or government entity), independent of any role it plays in a specific relationship.

label: Funder
definition: The role an organization occupies when it provides funding to grantees through grant programs and awards.

label: Grantee
definition: The role an organization occupies when it receives and administers grant funding awarded by a funder.

label: Fiscal Sponsor
definition: The role an organization occupies when it provides the legal and administrative infrastructure that lets another entity or project receive charitable funding on its behalf.
legalNote: Fiscal sponsorship arrangements vary significantly in legal structure (e.g., comprehensive/"Model A" vs. pre-approved grant relationship/"Model C"), which affects liability, employment, and asset ownership very differently. Consult counsel before relying on this model to characterize a specific arrangement.

label: Philanthropic Intermediary
definition: An organization commonly known for facilitating philanthropy on behalf of others -- such as by re-granting, fiscal sponsorship, or hosting donor-advised funds -- regardless of which specific role it occupies in a given arrangement.

label: Funding Intermediary Role
definition: The role an organization occupies when it channels funds between an original funding source and an ultimate grantee, without itself being the original funder or the final recipient.

label: Contractor
definition: The role an organization occupies when it is bound by a contract to deliver a specific, defined piece of work for another organization.

label: Vendor
definition: The role an organization occupies when it is the source from which another organization purchases standard goods or services, without a defined-work contract the way a Contractor has.

label: Service Provider
definition: The role an organization occupies when it provides an ongoing operational service to another organization -- broader and less transactional than a single Contractor engagement or Vendor purchase.

label: Employer
definition: The role an organization occupies when it employs a person -- the organization-side counterpart to that person's Employee role.

label: Partner
definition: The role an organization occupies when it collaborates with another organization on shared work, in a relationship not adequately described as one party purchasing from or providing a service to the other.

label: Sponsoring Organization
definition: The role an organization occupies when it holds and administers a Fund on behalf of the fund's donor or benefactors, distinct from acting as a Fiscal Sponsor for a specific project.

label: Program Officer
definition: The role a person occupies when they manage a portfolio of grants on behalf of a funder, from soliciting or reviewing applications through monitoring active awards.

label: Reviewer
definition: The role a person occupies when they evaluate an application against review criteria, whether as staff, a board member, or an external peer reviewer.

label: Grant Administrator
definition: The role a person occupies when they are responsible for compliance, reporting, and financial management of an award on behalf of the grantee organization.

label: Donor Advisor
definition: The role a person occupies when they hold non-binding privileges to recommend grants and investments from a Donor-Advised Fund, typically as the fund's original donor.
legalNote: A donor advisor's privileges are non-binding as a matter of federal tax law, not just convention -- treating a recommendation as a binding instruction can jeopardize the sponsoring organization's tax-exempt status.

label: Sponsored Project
definition: A project or group carrying out charitable activity under a Fiscal Sponsor's legal and administrative umbrella, without being itself an independent Organization.
legalNote: Whether a sponsored project's activities, staff, and liabilities legally belong to the fiscal sponsor depends entirely on the specific fiscal sponsorship model in use. This ontology does not distinguish between models -- consult the governing agreement.

label: Role
definition: A contextual capacity an agent occupies, distinct from the agent's permanent identity or classification.

label: Person
definition: A natural person who participates in nonprofit, philanthropic, governance, employment, advisory, or service relationships.

label: Person Role
definition: A contextual capacity a person occupies within an organization, award, application, agreement, arrangement, program, project, or other defined context.

label: Employee
definition: The role a person occupies when they work for and are compensated by an organization.

label: Board Member
definition: The role a person occupies when they serve on an organization's governing board.

label: Applicant Contact
definition: The role a person occupies when they serve as the primary point of contact for an application submitted on behalf of an organization or project.

label: Authorized Signatory
definition: The role a person occupies when they are authorized to sign a grant agreement or other governing document on behalf of an organization.

label: Donor
definition: The role a person occupies when they contribute charitable funds to an organization or fund, without necessarily holding advisory privileges over how they are used.

label: Consultant
definition: The role a person occupies when they provide paid, defined-scope services to an organization without being its employee.

label: Grant Program
definition: A funder's standing area of giving (e.g., "Environmental Justice Grants"), under which funding opportunities are issued over time.

label: Funding Opportunity
definition: A specific, time-bound invitation to apply for funding under a grant program, with defined eligibility, focus area, and deadlines.

label: Funding Cycle
definition: A recurring period (e.g., quarterly, annual) within a grant program during which applications are accepted and decided.

label: Eligibility Criteria
definition: The conditions an organization or project must meet to apply to a funding opportunity.

label: Budget
definition: A structured estimate of costs associated with a proposed or funded project, broken into categories (e.g., personnel, overhead, direct program costs).

label: Fund
definition: A designated pool of financial resources set aside for a purpose, distinct from the grant program or strategy that directs how it's used.

label: Donor-Advised Fund
definition: A Fund held by a sponsoring organization, over which a Donor Advisor holds non-binding privileges to recommend grants and investments.
legalNote: Donor-advised funds are subject to specific federal tax rules (e.g., IRC 4966-4967) governing what a donor advisor may and may not direct. This ontology models the general shape of the relationship, not compliance with those rules.

label: Philanthropic Arrangement
definition: A structured relationship among organizations that channels philanthropic funding outside a direct funder-to-grantee award -- such as a fiscal sponsorship or donor-advised fund arrangement.

label: Fiscal Sponsorship Arrangement
definition: A Philanthropic Arrangement in which a Fiscal Sponsor accepts and administers charitable funds on behalf of a Sponsored Project that lacks independent legal status to receive them directly.
legalNote: The rights and obligations created by a fiscal sponsorship agreement depend heavily on its specific model (e.g., comprehensive vs. pre-approved grant relationship). Consult counsel and the actual governing agreement rather than this ontology.

label: Donor-Advised Fund Arrangement
definition: A Philanthropic Arrangement in which a Donor Advisor holds non-binding advisory privileges over grants made from a Donor-Advised Fund.
legalNote: The specific privileges and limits granted to a donor advisor are set by the sponsoring organization's own policies and by tax law, not by this ontology -- consult counsel before using this model as a compliance reference.

label: Regranting Arrangement
definition: A Philanthropic Arrangement in which an organization receives funds and redistributes them to other organizations, acting as both a Grantee to the original source and a Funder or Funding Intermediary to the recipients.
legalNote: Regranting to organizations without their own tax-exempt status (or across borders) can trigger expenditure-responsibility or equivalency-determination requirements under U.S. tax law. This ontology does not model those compliance steps.

label: Collaborative Fund Arrangement
definition: A Philanthropic Arrangement in which multiple funders pool resources into a shared Fund and jointly direct or oversee its grantmaking.

label: Letter of Inquiry
definition: A brief, preliminary submission used by some funders to screen interest before inviting a full application.

label: Application
definition: A grantee's formal submission requesting funding under a specific funding opportunity, including a proposal narrative and budget.

label: Review
definition: The process of evaluating an application, producing a recommendation and often a score, conducted by one or more reviewers.

label: Review Criteria
definition: The published or internal standards (e.g., alignment with mission, feasibility, budget reasonableness) against which applications are scored.

label: Site Visit
definition: An optional step where a funder representative visits or meets with an applicant to assess capacity or verify claims before a decision.

label: Decision
definition: A recorded determination concerning an application following review or another authorized approval process. Its outcome (approved, declined, or approved with conditions) is carried by the decisionOutcome property, not by the Decision entity's identity itself.

label: Grant Recommendation
definition: A Donor Advisor's non-binding request that a Donor-Advised Fund make an award to a specific recipient; the fund's sponsoring organization retains final authority to accept or decline it.
legalNote: A Grant Recommendation's non-binding status is a legal requirement for donor-advised funds under federal tax law, not a design choice -- see Donor-Advised Fund and Donor Advisor.

label: Award
definition: A funder's formal commitment to provide a specific amount of funding to a grantee, following an approved application or decision.

label: Grant Agreement
definition: The legal document, signed by both funder and grantee, that formalizes an award's terms, conditions, and obligations.

label: Terms and Conditions
definition: The specific obligations, restrictions, and expectations attached to an award (e.g., allowable uses of funds, reporting requirements). Its own restrictionType property is a coarse restricted/unrestricted flag, superseded for new data by the structured Use Restriction model (see Grant Term) -- retained for backward compatibility.

label: Restricted Funding
definition: Funding that must be used for a specific purpose, project, or time period defined in the grant agreement. Deprecated: prefer Fund's restrictionType property, backed by the restriction-type reference scheme, for new data -- retained for backward compatibility.

label: Unrestricted Funding
definition: Funding a grantee may use at its discretion in support of its general mission. Deprecated: prefer Fund's restrictionType property, backed by the restriction-type reference scheme, for new data -- retained for backward compatibility.

label: Matching Requirement
definition: A condition requiring the grantee to raise or contribute additional funds alongside the award, often as a ratio (e.g., 1:1 match).

label: Amendment
definition: A formally agreed change to an existing grant agreement's terms, budget, timeline, or amount, made after the original agreement was signed.

label: Grant Term
definition: A provision associated with a Grant Agreement or Award that establishes a restriction, condition, obligation, approval requirement, reporting requirement, or other requirement governing the use, administration, performance, or continuation of grant funding. Preserves its original source wording (via originalTermText) alongside its normalized classification -- the classification is an interpretation of the source text, not a replacement for it.

label: Use Restriction
definition: A Grant Term limiting the purposes, activities, populations, geographies, time periods, cost categories, or other uses for which grant resources may be applied. Governs permitted use -- distinct from a Grant Condition, which governs whether some entitlement, payment, or continuation becomes effective.

label: Grant Condition
definition: A Grant Term establishing a barrier, milestone, event, requirement, or other criterion that must be satisfied for grant entitlement, payment, continuation, release, or retention. Matching Requirement and Payment Condition are its existing concrete subtypes. A condition's barrier facts (e.g. hasBarrier, threshold) are captured here without the ontology itself making the accounting or legal determination of whether the grant is "conditional".

label: Approval Requirement
definition: A Grant Term requiring authorization from the funder or another specified party before a defined change, expenditure, action, or deviation may occur (e.g., prior written approval for a budget reallocation above a threshold). Not automatically a Grant Condition -- an approval requirement may simply govern administration of the Award.

label: Reporting Requirement
definition: A Grant Term requiring submission of information concerning grant activities, finances, progress, outputs, outcomes, compliance, or closeout. Finer-grained than a Reporting Schedule (which sets the overall cadence for an award): one clause such as "quarterly programmatic and financial reports are required" normalizes into two Reporting Requirements, one per report type, each of which may be fulfilledBy a submitted Report.

label: Payment Schedule
definition: The agreed timing and amounts by which award funds will be disbursed to the grantee.

label: Installment
definition: A single scheduled portion of an award's total funds, to be disbursed at a defined point or upon meeting a condition.

label: Payment
definition: An actual transfer of funds from funder to grantee against an award, corresponding to one or more installments.

label: Payment Condition
definition: A requirement (e.g., a submitted report, a milestone reached) that must be satisfied before a scheduled payment is released.

label: Budget Modification
definition: A grantee-requested, funder-approved change to how awarded funds are allocated across budget categories, without changing the total award amount.

label: Compliance Requirement
definition: An obligation attached to an award that the grantee must satisfy to remain in good standing (e.g., timely reporting, allowable use of funds, insurance).

label: Reporting Schedule
definition: The agreed cadence and due dates for narrative and financial reports over the life of an award.

label: Report
definition: A grantee's submission to the funder describing progress, outcomes, and/or use of funds, per the reporting schedule. Narrative and financial reports are common subtypes.

label: Audit
definition: A formal, independent examination of a grantee's financial records, either as a general organizational requirement or specific to a grant.

label: Indirect Cost Rate
definition: The negotiated or de minimis rate at which a grantee may charge overhead/administrative costs against an award.

label: Theory of Change
definition: A grantee's or funder's articulated model of how specific activities are expected to lead to desired long-term change.

label: Logic Model
definition: A structured diagram connecting a project's inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes, used to plan and evaluate a grant-funded project.

label: Output
definition: A direct product, service, deliverable, or immediate consequence of Activities carried out by a Project (e.g., number of workshops held, people served). Does not itself imply any broader behavioral or social change.

label: Outcome
definition: A change in condition, behavior, knowledge, capacity, practice, or status that is intended or observed in association with a Project or Activity, distinct from a direct Output. A recorded Outcome does not by itself establish that the Project caused it -- see Evidence Claim for how a specific causal or contributory interpretation is represented and evidenced.

label: Result
definition: A planned or observed state, product, change, or effect associated with an intervention. Output, Outcome, and Impact are its three subtypes, distinguished by directness and time horizon.

label: Impact
definition: A broader or longer-term change to which one or more Outcomes may contribute. An Impact relationship does not itself imply that the Project has been demonstrated to cause the change.

label: Input
definition: A financial, human, material, informational, or other resource used in carrying out an Activity.

label: Activity
definition: A defined action or body of work performed by a Project to produce Outputs and contribute toward intended Outcomes.

label: Indicator
definition: A defined measure used to assess the state or change of a Result (e.g., percentage of participants employed after six months, graduation rate).

label: Target
definition: A planned value for an Indicator expected to be reached by a defined point in time.

label: Measurement
definition: An observed value for an Indicator at a particular time and, where relevant, for a defined Population or Geographic Area. Never treated as interchangeable with a Target: a Target is planned, a Measurement is observed.

label: Evidence
definition: Information used to support, weaken, qualify, or contextualize a claim about a Project, Activity, Result, or other entity (e.g., an evaluation report, survey results, administrative data, a case study).

label: Evidence Claim
definition: A sourced assertion about a relationship, condition, result, or causal interpretation whose evidentiary basis can be independently identified. This is where a specific interpretation of a Project's contribution to a Result -- association, contribution, attribution, or causation -- is represented, distinct from the Result itself and from the Evidence supporting the claim.

label: Evaluation
definition: A structured assessment of whether a grant-funded project achieved its intended outputs and outcomes.

label: Closeout
definition: The formal conclusion of a grant award once all funds are disbursed, all reports are submitted and accepted, and all compliance requirements are satisfied.

label: Grant Lifecycle
definition: The end-to-end sequence a grant moves through, from funding opportunity through application, review, award, disbursement, reporting, and closeout.

label: Agent
definition: An entity capable of participating in an activity, relationship, decision, transaction, or role. Person and Organization are its two subtypes.

label: Project
definition: A defined body of work undertaken over a period of time to address one or more needs or objectives -- the work being performed, distinct from the Application requesting funding for it or the Award committing funding to it.

label: Classification Assignment
definition: A contextual assertion that a resource (e.g. an Award or Population) is classified by a concept from a specified external or internal classification scheme, such as Candid's Philanthropy Classification System. External taxonomies classify CommonGood resources; they do not define those resources -- Need, Population, and Organization remain the ontology's own entities regardless of which taxonomy terms are assigned to them.

label: Need
definition: A condition, problem, gap, or opportunity identified as warranting intervention or investment.

label: Population
definition: A group of people defined by demographic, geographic, institutional, experiential, or other characteristics relevant to a Need, Project, Result, or Evaluation.

label: Geographic Area
definition: A geographic entity used to describe where a Need exists, where a Project operates, where a Population is located, or where a Result is observed.
